verdict.rationale: cubic documents several first-party natural-language control surfaces. In PR comments you can ask questions, trigger reviews and request fixes ("@cubic-dev-ai review this PR"), and a chat sidebar accepts requests like "tour this PR". Through its MCP server, a coding agent can request reviews, triage issues and manage subscription seats and roles conversationally. missing for 10: no evidence that configuration (cubic.yaml, custom agents, auto-approval settings) can be changed by natural language, and no independent or hands-on corroboration of the natural-language command surfaces.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Interact with cubic in PR comments to ask questions, trigger reviews, and fix issues.
Ask chat to "tour this PR" for a step-by-step review of the changes and what to check.
You can now ask your coding agent to check your cubic subscription, manage team seats and roles, and purchase more seats without leaving your MCP client.
Connect cubic's MCP server to your coding agent to read review findings and codebase context, request PR reviews, and triage PR or codebase scan issues.
Reply to a review comment to ask for clarification
